Char: Patient sampling:
"All patients coming to the clinics were visited with a recent (less than 1 month old) routine blood analysis and abdominal ultrasonography (US) ordered by either the community referring physician or by the usual treating doctor from our Unit. Liver surface was assessed using high-frequency (5–10 MHz) broadband linear array transducers. Spleen size was determined as spleen bipolar diameter (across the spleen hilium), using multifrequency (1–8 MHz) convex probes. Splenomegaly was defined as spleen diameter over 12 cm. The consistency of ultrasound parameters was further verified independently by 2 of the investigators (SA, JG), who reviewed all the patient’s US images at the moment of the first visit."

"At baseline (the moment of the first visit), all patients underwent a regular consultation (review of medical history, current symptoms and physical examination). Exclusion criteria to enter the study were: (1) past or present episode of clinical decompensation (ascites, variceal hemorrhage or hepatic encephalopathy); (2) known esophageal varices; (3) known hepatocellular carcinoma; and/ or (4) evident collateral circulation on previous imaging studies. If none of these criteria were met, the patient was asked to be included in the study cohort and to undergo a liver stiffness (LS) measurement through TE (Fibroscan, Echosens, Paris, France) performed by a single operator with experience in more than 500 procedures (LM). Only those Patients with LS P13.6 kPa entered the diagnostic study and were further evaluated by upper endoscopy and HVPG measurement. Both procedures were performed according to the standard of practice in our center as described previously and in accordance with the recommended standards."
Char: Patient characteristics and settin: "A prospective, longitudinal, single-center observational study was performed to evaluate the feasibility and accuracy of a systematic strategy based on simple routine parameters and LS measurements, with the specific aim of identifying patients with portal hypertension in an early phase (i.e., without high-risk varices) among a large cohort of all consecutive patients with asymptomatic chronic liver disease in an outpatient clinical setting. For this purpose, we considered all consecutive patients with chronic liver disease coming to our outpatient clinics between January 2010 and April 2012. Our outpatient clinics are part of a specialized Liver Unit in a tertiary university hospital in downtown Barcelona, Spain, that serves as the reference center for chronic liver disease (including cirrhosis and its complications) for an area with a population of approximately 450,000 people."

Char: Patient sampling: "A total of 141 newly diagnosed patients with HCV-related chronic liver disease were consecutively considered for inclusion in the study. Of these, 11 were excluded because of the presence of complications (2 hepatocellular carcinoma, 1 portal vein thrombosis, 5 moderate-severe ascites, 3 esophageal bleeding) and 17 were excluded because the diagnosis of cirrhosis was not confirmed at histopathologic examination. Therefore, a total of 113 patients with HCV-related cirrhosis without clinically evident complications, mainly the presence of significant ascites known to limit the performance of TE, were finally enrolled. Patients were accurately selected using clinical, biochemical (platelet count, international normalized ratio, prothrombin time, aspartate aminotransferase [AST], alanine aminotransferase [ALT], albumin, bilirubin, pseudocholinesterase, total cholesterol), and US parameters (ie, liver margins; size of left, right, and caudate lobes; spleen bipolar diameter; anteroposterior diameter of the portal trunk; portal vein flow; hepatic vein flow; and resistance index). Liver biopsy was necessary in 22 cases (19.5%) to confirm the diagnosis of cirrhosis. No patient enrolled in the study had significant ascites at clinical examination, acute liver disease, coinfection with hepatitis B virus or human immunodeficiency virus, metabolic liver disease, autoimmune hepatitis, or biliary tract disorders. Furthermore, no patient was under treatment with antivirals, beta-blockers, or diuretics at the time of the study. The presence of alcohol abuse within the 6 months preceding the study was excluded in all patients. In addition, clinical conditions potentially affecting TE (eg, cardiac failure) or in which this technique is contraindicated (eg, pregnancy) were also excluded."

Patients who were on NSBB at the time of HVPG measurement but exhibited HVPG ≥10 mmHg and had varices were included. The 20 included Hanoverian patients underwent HVPG and NIT assessment as part of the prospective, observational IMPRHOVE-D study. The 31 included Viennese patients were identified by manual search of the local Viennese HVPG database. SSM was conducted and available in all Viennese patients who underwent prospective characterization after 2019 (n=20)."
Char: Patient characteristics and settin: "All HBV/HDV-coinfected, i.e., anti-HDV seropositive, cACLD (LSM ≥10 kPa and/or METAVIR F3/4 fibrosis on histology) patients without previous hepatic decompensation who underwent prospective characterization by paired HVPG and non-invasive test (NIT) assessment at the Vienna Hepatic Hemodynamic Lab of the Medical University of Vienna or at Hannover Medical School between 2013 and 2023 were retrospectively included in the main cohort and analyzed. Fifty-three HBV/HDV-cACLD patients were screened for inclusion in the main cohort. One patient was excluded owing to unreliable HVPG results due to vein-vein communications. Another patient was excluded because of ongoing NSBB treatment and HVPG levels below 10 mmHg. Ultimately, the final study cohort comprised 51 patients (n=31 from Vienna, n=20 from Hannover). Char: Index test: "LSM was assessed by VCTE (FibroScan, Echosens, Paris, France) according to international recommendations that were followed in both centers. Char: Target condition and reference sta: "HVPG measurements were conducted in fasting condition according to international recommendations. Briefly, upon punction of the right internal jugular vein under local anesthesia, free and wedged hepatic venous pressure were measured in triplicate. HVPG was obtained by subtracting the free hepatic venous pressure from wedged hepatic venous pressure, and the mean of three measurements represented the final value. CSPH was defined as HVPG ≥10 mmHg."
